synopsis: Sweden’s EVIDENT program, associated with SAFER and Vinnova, ran from April 2022 to December 2024—about 33 months—to develop simulation credibility methods [f1206, f1553, f15710, f1459]. It researched credible virtual driver-assistance and automated-driving verification, correlation, and replacing or complementing real recordings; the VaViM/EVIDENT comparison describes literature studies, feasibility models, comparative physical tests, and validated models used alongside real tests [f1554, f15711, f1926, f1931]. The booklet uses EVIDENT and other publicly funded programs as a schedule-forecasting reference class, concluding that building validation capability, including rigorous credibility methodology, takes years [f15692, f15717, f15713, f1555]. The comparison lists a six-month pre-study capability-building period and a 33-month EVIDENT capability-building period, but marks validation time after capability became available as not applicable, leaving no separate operational validation-duration benchmark [f1927, f1928, f1930]. Funders accepted the VaViM/EVIDENT evidence, but there was no approval, so this precedent demonstrates research credibility rather than an approval outcome [f1932].
